investigation.title: MER-87: Issue created: Switch invoice date handling to UTC
investigation.escalationText: Meridian reports that invoice totals have been wrong since release 4.12, our finance team is blocked, and we have not had a reply to four messages. Please explain what happened and when this will be fixed. We need a written explanation and a firm fix date today.
investigation.plan:
Meridian reports invoice totals wrong since release 4.12, finance blocked, and four unanswered messages, demanding a written explanation and firm fix date. The event store (jira + slack, 2024-09-05 to 2024-09-30) centers on a UTC invoice-date change (MER-87) suspected as the cause (MER-101), with a Sep 24 fix attempt that QA reportedly failed and an unresolved Resolved status; the plan below frames what investigators must verify before any explanation or date is offered.

Hypotheses to test:
- The MER-87 UTC invoice-date change at 4.12 introduced the totals/timeline error seen in MER-101. — test: Trace 4.12 build/deploy timing against MER-87 status transitions and MER-101 creation; compare pre/post-4.12 invoice date-handling change records and reproduce totals in test on 4.12 vs prior build.; falsify: Show invoice totals were already wrong before the MER-87 change shipped in 4.12, or that 4.12 did not include the MER-87 date-handling change.
- The Sep 24 fix release did not resolve the totals defect (QA still off by a day), so the Resolved status on MER-101 is premature/incorrect. — test: Pull Sep 24 build test results and QA notes in meridian-billing; compare the MER-101 Resolved transition (Sep 26) to evidence of a passing fix; verify what build Meridian actually received.; falsify: Produce passing QA evidence on the Sep 24 build plus a deployed fix that corrects totals, showing the Resolved status is accurate.
- Meridian's four unanswered messages stem from an ownership gap—Lin Chen on leave until Oct 2 with no handoff on MER-101—leaving the client without a responder. — test: Map each Meridian inbound message to a responder and response; inspect meridian-billing for handoff/assignment changes around Sep 20 and any reassignment to Dana/Marcus.; falsify: Find timely replies to all four Meridian messages, or evidence that ownership was formally reassigned before Lin Chen's leave.
- The totals error is a date/timezone boundary artifact (off-by-a-day) affecting some invoices rather than all totals computation. — test: Isolate failing invoices and check whether the discrepancy is consistently ±1 day at a date boundary; compare invoices near month/day boundaries vs interior dates.; falsify: Find total mismatches that are not date-boundary shifts (e.g., amount arithmetic errors) or that occur on non-boundary dates.
- There is a second, independent defect (e.g., the MER-104 nightly export retry or an export/dependency change) contributing to wrong totals separate from the timezone issue. — test: Review MER-104 and any export/dependency changes in the window; test whether retry/export behavior alters or duplicates totals independently of the date change.; falsify: Show export/retry path is inert for invoice totals or that correcting the timezone alone fully reconciles Meridian totals.

Seed terms: MER-101, MER-87, MER-102, MER-104, 4.12, meridian-billing, meridian, invoice, totals, wrong, invoice date, UTC, timezone, off by a day, date handling, release, build, bump, fix, fix date

People to look at: Marcus Webb, Dana Okoro, Lin Chen, Priya Nair

Focus window: 2024-09-05 → 2024-09-30

Unknowns to keep open:
- Which specific 4.12 build/deploy date and contents; whether MER-87 shipped exactly in 4.12.
- What the four unanswered Meridian messages were, their dates, and channels used.
- Whether any client-facing reply or fix date was previously promised.
- Whether the Sep 24 build was ever deployed to Meridian and what Meridian currently runs.
- Why MER-101 was marked Resolved on Sep 26 despite QA failure on Sep 25.
- Who currently owns MER-101 given Lin Chen's leave until Oct 2 and lack of handoff.
- Whether MER-102 and MER-104 are related or independent of the totals defect.
- Scope of impact: how many Meridian invoices/totals are affected and whether it is a consistent off-by-one-day shift.

claims.text: MER-87's UTC invoice-date change was merged to release branch 4.12 and 4.12 went live on production on Sep 10, the same morning Meridian reported invoice totals wrong since the 4.12 deploy — supporting MER-87 as the introducing change.
claims.quote: Merged to release branch 4.12; invoices now use a UTC conversion.

claims.text: Marcus Webb attributed the Meridian totals defect to the MER-87 timezone change and committed the fix to the Sep 24 release, both in MER-101 and in the meridian-billing channel.
claims.quote: Root cause looks like the MER-87 timezone change. Fix scheduled for the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: QA (Dana Okoro) reported the Sep 24 build still failing with totals off by a day in test, i.e. the fix Marcus committed to the Sep 24 release did not correct the defect.
claims.quote: QA is still failing on the Sep 24 build; totals are off by a day in test.

claims.text: Marcus Webb himself committed on Sep 25 to keeping MER-101 open until QA passed, then reversed that decision on Sep 26 by marking it resolved over QA's objection.
claims.quote: Let us keep MER-101 open until QA passes.

claims.text: Marcus Webb marked MER-101 resolved asserting the fix was in the Sep 24 build, despite QA having failed that same build the day before; Dana Okoro objected that the fix was not in the build she tested.
claims.quote: Marking MER-101 resolved; the fix is in the Sep 24 build.

claims.text: Lin Chen left until Oct 2 with no handoff arranged for MER-101, creating an unanswered ownership gap for the Meridian defect while it remained open.
claims.quote: I am on leave until Oct 2. No handoff set up yet for MER-101.

claims.text: At the end of the window there is still no evidence of a client-facing resolution: Marcus Webb on Sep 30 was still asking whether anyone had heard back from the client about the totals.
claims.quote: Has anyone heard back from Northwind about the totals?

claims.text: No evidence ties the other changes in the window to the totals error: MER-104 was only a nightly export retry and MER-102 a routine PDF renderer dependency bump with no customer impact, both recorded independently before MER-101 was raised.
claims.quote: Nightly export retries twice now.

claims.text: Marcus Webb confirmed 4.12 was live on production on Sep 10, the deployment boundary against which Meridian's 'since 4.12' report is dated.
claims.quote: 4.12 is live on production as of this morning.

claims.text: Marcus Webb declared the Sep 24 release cut with the invoice fix included, but QA failed the build and never confirmed a passing fix was ever shipped to Meridian.
claims.quote: Sep 24 release is cut; invoice fix included.

claims.text: The client issue was acknowledged internally on Sep 12 in meridian-billing, but MER-101 itself was not moved to In Progress until Sep 23 — an 11-day delay before anyone owned the fix.
claims.quote: Meridian flagged wrong invoice totals; looking at MER-101.

claims.text: MER-87 changed invoice date handling to UTC and was merged to release branch 4.12 by Lin Chen on Sep 10 03:00.
claims.quote: Merged to release branch 4.12; invoices now use a UTC conversion.

claims.text: 4.12 went live on production on the morning of Sep 10, the same day the MER-87 UTC change was merged, and the totals defect was reported on Sep 10 after that deploy.
claims.quote: 4.12 is live on production as of this morning.

claims.text: The reported symptom is an apparent off-by-a-day shift: Meridian reports invoice totals are wrong since the 4.12 deploy, with timelines off by a day.
claims.quote: Meridian reports invoice totals are wrong since the 4.12 deploy; timelines are off by a day.

claims.text: Marcus Webb attributed the wrong totals to the MER-87 timezone change and scheduled a fix for the Sep 24 release.
claims.quote: Root cause looks like the MER-87 timezone change. Fix scheduled for the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: Marcus Webb stated the Sep 24 release was cut with the invoice fix included.
claims.quote: Sep 24 release is cut; invoice fix included.

claims.text: QA on the Sep 24 build still failed, with totals off by a day in test.
claims.quote: QA is still failing on the Sep 24 build; totals are off by a day in test.

claims.text: Marcus Webb had decided to keep MER-101 open until QA passed, the day before it was marked Resolved.
claims.quote: Let us keep MER-101 open until QA passes.

claims.text: On Sep 26 Marcus Webb announced marking MER-101 resolved because the fix was in the Sep 24 build, despite QA failure the prior day.
claims.quote: Marking MER-101 resolved; the fix is in the Sep 24 build.

claims.text: Dana Okoro objected that the fix was not in the build she tested, yet the Resolved status stood.
claims.quote: It is not in the build I tested, but ok.

claims.text: MER-101 was transitioned In Progress → Resolved on Sep 26 02:00 with no evidence of a passing QA fix.
claims.quote: Status: In Progress → Resolved

claims.text: Lin Chen went on leave until Oct 2 with no handoff set up for MER-101 (stated Sep 20).
claims.quote: I am on leave until Oct 2. No handoff set up yet for MER-101.

claims.text: Prior to the MER-101 ticket, the only acknowledgement of Meridian's complaint was Marcus Webb saying he was looking at MER-101 (Sep 12), three days after the issue was created.
claims.quote: Meridian flagged wrong invoice totals; looking at MER-101.

claims.text: MER-104 (nightly export retry, created Sep 7) was recorded as a retry addition only, with no evidence linking it to invoice totals.
claims.quote: Nightly export retries twice now.

claims.text: MER-102 (PDF renderer dependency bump) was explicitly characterized as having no customer impact, so it is not a candidate cause for the totals error.
claims.quote: Routine dependency bump, no customer impact.

claims.text: Marcus Webb also told the team on Sep 23 in meridian-billing that the MER-87 timezone change was the cause with the fix targeted at the Sep 24 release.
claims.quote: MER-87 timezone change is the cause. Fix targeted at the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: As of Sep 30 08:00 the status of client communication was still open inside the team, with Marcus Webb asking whether anyone had heard back about the totals.
claims.quote: Has anyone heard back from Northwind about the totals?

claims.text: Lin Chen committed that the UTC invoice-date handling change would ship in release branch 4.12 ("Merged to release branch 4.12; invoices now use a UTC conversion"); 4.12 was live on production on 2024-09-10, and Meridian reported wrong totals "since the 4.12 deploy", so the change did ship in 4.12.
claims.quote: Merged to release branch 4.12; invoices now use a UTC conversion.

claims.text: Marcus Webb committed on MER-101 that a fix for the totals defect was scheduled for the Sep 24 release; the Sep 24 release was cut with the invoice fix included, so the release-timing promise was met.
claims.quote: Root cause looks like the MER-87 timezone change. Fix scheduled for the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: Marcus Webb stated in meridian-billing that the MER-87 timezone fix was targeted at the Sep 24 release, and later confirmed "Sep 24 release is cut; invoice fix included." — the targeted release did occur.
claims.quote: MER-87 timezone change is the cause. Fix targeted at the Sep 24 release.

claims.text: Marcus Webb committed in meridian-billing to keep MER-101 open until QA passes ("Let us keep MER-101 open until QA passes."), but the very next day, after Dana Okoro reported QA still failing, MER-101 was transitioned to Resolved on 2024-09-26 — the promise was broken.
claims.quote: Let us keep MER-101 open until QA passes.

claims.text: Marcus Webb asserted in meridian-billing "Marking MER-101 resolved; the fix is in the Sep 24 build," but Dana Okoro immediately replied "It is not in the build I tested, but ok." and QA had reported the Sep 24 build still failing, so the claim underpinning the resolution was not substantiated.
claims.quote: Marking MER-101 resolved; the fix is in the Sep 24 build.

claims.text: Dana Okoro stated that QA is still failing on the Sep 24 build with totals off by a day in test, contradicting Marcus Webb's assertion that the Sep 24 build contains a working fix; this QA result directly falsifies the passing-fix condition for resolving MER-101.
claims.quote: QA is still failing on the Sep 24 build; totals are off by a day in test.

claims.text: Lin Chen, owner of MER-101's date-handling work, announced on 2024-09-20 in meridian-billing that they were on leave until Oct 2 with no handoff set up for MER-101, leaving the Meridian issue without a named responder across the Sep 24–30 window.
claims.quote: I am on leave until Oct 2. No handoff set up yet for MER-101.

claims.text: Priya Nair recorded that Meridian reports invoice totals wrong since the 4.12 deploy with timelines off by a day, and the MER-87 UTC conversion was merged into 4.12 — consistent with the timezone/date-boundary artifact as cause.
claims.quote: Meridian reports invoice totals are wrong since the 4.12 deploy; timelines are off by a day.

claims.text: MER-101 was transitioned In Progress → Resolved on 2024-09-26 by Marcus Webb one day after QA failure was reported and one day after he committed to keep it open until QA passes, making the Resolved status premature.
claims.quote: Status: In Progress → Resolved

claims.text: As of 2024-09-30, the last record in meridian-billing shows Marcus Webb still asking whether anyone had heard back from the client, indicating no client-facing written explanation or fix date had been delivered by end of window.
claims.quote: Has anyone heard back from Northwind about the totals?

claims.text: Dana Okoro documented MER-102 as a routine PDF renderer dependency bump with no customer impact, and MER-104 as adding two retries to the nightly export; neither record links them to the Meridian totals defect, so no independent export/dependency defect is evidenced in the registry.
claims.quote: Routine dependency bump, no customer impact.

The cited event records QA still failing on the Sep 24 build; it does not establish that 'the fix Marcus committed to the Sep 24 release did not correct the defect' — we have no evidence the fix was actually present in that build (Dana later says it was not in the build she tested). Lin Chen left until Oct 2 with no handoff arranged for MER-101, creating an unanswered ownership gap for the Meridian defect while it remained open.
